title: Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: EVAP purge flow sensor reading inconsistent with commanded purge.
fullDescription:
P0466 sets when the dedicated purge flow sensor (used on some larger displacement engines) does not track commanded purge duty cycle. The PCM relies on this sensor to confirm the canister is being properly evacuated.

Without valid purge flow data the EVAP monitor cannot complete and the OBD readiness flag will not set.
safetyImpact: None directly; emissions readiness affected.

fixSteps.title: Compare commanded vs measured purge
fixSteps.instruction: Use scanner data on monitor run.

faq.q: Where is this sensor?
faq.a: In the purge line between the canister and intake on equipped vehicles.

title: Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Low Input
shortDescription: Purge flow sensor signal below minimum.
fullDescription:
P0467 sets when the purge flow sensor signal stays below the lower threshold under conditions that should produce flow. Either there is no flow (mechanical) or the sensor reads low (electrical).

Distinguishing the two requires watching the signal during a commanded purge cycle.
safetyImpact: None.

faq.q: Is purge flow same as MAF?
faq.a: No — separate sensor specifically for canister purge volume.

title: Cooling Fan Rationality Check Failure
shortDescription: Cooling fan response does not match command across operating range.
fullDescription:
P0483 is part of the cooling fan circuit monitor family. Modern PWM-controlled fans report speed feedback to the PCM; deviation from command sets these codes.

With a fan fault the PCM may default to commanded full-on, sometimes leading to a fan that runs constantly even with the engine cold.
safetyImpact: Possible overheating risk if fan stuck off; battery drain if stuck on.

causes.cause: Failed fan motor or PWM module

fixSteps.title: Check fan module / relay
fixSteps.instruction: Test PWM signal and battery feed.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Most modern fans sold as motor+module unit.

faq.q: Can I run without the fan briefly?
faq.a: In cold weather highway driving yes; in stop-and-go traffic the engine will overheat fast.

title: Starter Request Circuit
shortDescription: Starter request signal from BCM/ignition is invalid.
fullDescription:
P0512 indicates the PCM did not see the expected starter request from the ignition switch / BCM during a crank attempt, or saw it during conditions when it should not have been present (such as while running).

On push-button vehicles this often points to a BCM-PCM communication issue rather than a switch fault.
safetyImpact: Possible no-crank condition.

causes.cause: Wiring open/short on start request line

fixSteps.title: Read BCM start-request status
fixSteps.instruction: Should toggle when key turned to START.

faq.q: Why no-start with this code?
faq.a: The PCM disables fueling until it sees a valid start request.

title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Battery temperature sensor reading implausible vs ambient.
fullDescription: P0514 affects either the smart-charging system (battery temp sensor enables temperature-compensated voltage) or the idle air control loop on older throttle-body equipped engines. Battery temperature codes are common with ECMs that no longer support legacy sensor; idle codes typically reflect carbon buildup or motor wear.
safetyImpact: Idle stalls possible; charging system slightly less optimal.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body (idle codes)
fixSteps.instruction: Carbon removal often resolves idle codes.

faq.q: Battery temp sensor — where is it?
faq.a: Typically on or near the battery in the engine bay or trunk.

title: Intake Air Heater 'A' Circuit Low
shortDescription: Diesel intake air heater control signal stuck low.
fullDescription:
P0541 affects the intake grid heater used on diesels for cold starting. The heater is a high-current resistive grid in the intake manifold that warms inducted air below ~5°C.

A stuck-on heater drains the battery quickly; a stuck-off heater causes hard cold starts and white-smoke in cold weather.
safetyImpact: Hard cold starts; potential battery drain.

fixSteps.title: Check heater current draw
fixSteps.instruction: Should pull 100-200 A briefly during preheat.

faq.q: Are intake heaters and glow plugs the same?
faq.a: No — heaters warm intake air; glow plugs heat the combustion chamber.

title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: PS pressure sensor reading does not track steering input.
fullDescription:
P0551 reflects a sensor input the PCM uses for engine load compensation (PS) or for brake booster vacuum monitoring on engines that don't run continuous high vacuum (turbo, hybrid, start-stop).

On equipped vehicles this code can be why start-stop won't activate or why the engine briefly runs to refill brake vacuum.
safetyImpact: Possible idle dip with PS load if engine cannot compensate.
symptoms: Possible engine restart at stop (booster codes)

fixSteps.title: Check vacuum integrity (booster)
fixSteps.instruction: Booster should hold vacuum after engine off.

faq.q: Why does this affect start-stop?
faq.a: Without valid booster vacuum data the system disables auto-stop for safety.

title: Vehicle Speed Output Circuit
shortDescription: Vehicle speed output signal from PCM to other modules is faulty.
fullDescription:
P0609 affects either internal PCM/TCM operation or the smart-charging communication between PCM and alternator. Modern alternators use PWM field control commanded by the PCM rather than a self-regulating internal regulator.

A fault here can cause overcharging, undercharging, or simply prevent the charge lamp from working as a warning.
safetyImpact: Possible battery damage from over/undercharge.

causes.cause: Wiring fault between PCM and alternator

fixSteps.title: Scope field control signal
fixSteps.instruction: PWM duty cycle should respond to load.

faq.q: Why does my battery die overnight?
faq.a: If field is stuck on the alternator can backdrive and drain the battery; if stuck off the battery never recharges.
